prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1433; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers responded to a report of a two-vehicle collision in Houston, Texas, involving a low-speed head-on impact. On arrival, Driver 1 was standing beside a sedan with the front bumper and hood pushed in, and Driver 2 was seated in a second vehicle with visible front-end damage. Driver 1 reported neck pain and stiffness consistent with whiplash and said the impact had jolted the head forward and back. Driver 2 gave a statement that matched Driver 1's account of how the vehicles came together, and two independent witnesses on the scene described the same sequence. Photographs taken at the scene show damage that corresponds with the reported point and force of impact, and no prior damage to either vehicle was noted by anyone present. A Passenger seated in the rear of Driver 1's vehicle was identified by both witnesses and confirmed being in the car at the time of the crash. Driver 1 was confirmed as a named driver on the insurance policy covering the sedan. Officers observed no signs of impairment and recorded the scene for the file.
